summary: Traces masculinity gurus from Robert Bly's 1990s mythopoetic men's movement to Andrew Tate, the kickboxer turned influencer who ran an exploitative webcam business, sold Hustlers University to boys and was arrested in Romania in 2022 on trafficking charges.

evidence.note: Bly's first poetry collection, 1962, opens his career narrative
Bly's late-1960s anti-Vietnam War activism and essay discussed at length
Bly's Iron John workshops as the start of the modern men's self-help industry
Tate born in Washington, DC, in December 1986
Kickboxing career and padded record examined, plus childhood chess
Webcam business started 2012; brothers move to Romania in 2015
Rape and strangulation allegations in the UK and police inaction
Tate joins the post-2016 far-right influencer scene, Infowars, Tommy Robinson tactics
Tate messaged 16-year-old Romanian schoolgirls on Instagram
Followers paid to post clip compilations to game TikTok's algorithm
Late-2022 arrest in Romania with Tristan on trafficking accusations
UK schools holding deradicalisation sessions for boys, sets reaches_present

notes: Mythopoetic movement is in the title but gets one of four parts, so kept secondary. Covered span starts with Bly's 1962 debut; his birth is a single line. Main span ends at the December 2022 arrest. child-abuse theme left out: the DMs to 16-year-olds and child-labour advice are short segments; reviewer may add it. Greece march and Bly's US workshops not given extra setting codes beyond US.
